claims.statement: In Indonesian mythology, the sundel bolong is a ghost of the archipelago, a woman with beautiful long black hair and a long white dress, similar to the pontianak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Indonesia, sundel bolong adalah hantu dari Nusantara berupa perempuan berambut panjang hitam yang indah dan bergaun putih panjang, mirip pontianak.
claims.quote: In Indonesian mythology, a sundel bolong is a mythical ghost from the archipelago which is a woman with beautiful long, black hair and a long white dress (her form is similar to Pontianak).

claims.statement: The myth is tied to prostitutes; the name means 'prostitute with a hole', referring to the large hole in her back.
claims.statement_id: Mitos ini terkait erat dengan pelacur; namanya berarti 'pelacur yang berlubang', merujuk lubang besar di punggungnya.
claims.quote: The myth is closely linked to prostitutes, meaning a "prostitute with a hole in her", in reference to the large hole which is said to appear in her back.

claims.statement: The sundel bolong is the soul of a woman who died pregnant outside marriage and gave birth in her grave, or who died in childbirth with the baby coming out of her back.
claims.statement_id: Sundel bolong adalah arwah perempuan yang mati saat hamil di luar nikah sehingga melahirkan di kubur, atau yang mati saat bersalin dengan bayi keluar dari punggungnya.
claims.quote: is the soul of a woman who died when she was pregnant outside of marriage and therefore gave birth in her grave, or who died during childbirth and the baby came out from her back

claims.statement: Her victims are mainly men and children; as a vengeful spirit she is said to castrate men who reject her and take newborns to replace her lost child.
claims.statement_id: Korban sundel bolong terutama laki-laki dan anak-anak; sebagai arwah pendendam ia dikatakan mengebiri laki-laki yang menolaknya dan mengambil bayi baru lahir sebagai pengganti anaknya.
claims.quote: The victims of sundel bolong supposedly consist mainly of men and children. As a vengeful spirit, if rejected by a man, she is said to castrate him. Children, especially newborns are said to be taken to replace her lost child.

claims.statement: The sundel bolong (Malay: sundal bolong) is also called Buruk Punggung in Belitung; many think she is the kuntilanak, as both have long hair and white dresses, but her back has a hole.
claims.statement_id: Sundel bolong (Melayu: sundal bolong) juga disebut Buruk Punggung di Belitung; banyak yang menyangkanya sama dengan kuntilanak karena sama-sama berambut panjang dan bergaun putih, tetapi punggungnya berlubang.
claims.quote: Nama lainnya adalah Buruk Punggung (Belitung) Banyak yang menyangka bahwa Sundel Bolong sama dengan Kuntilanak, karena dalam mitosnya, keduanya digambarkan sama-sama berambut panjang dan mengenakan gaun putih. Hal yang membedakan antara penggambaran sundel bolong dengan kuntilanak adalah punggungnya yang bolong (berlubang).

claims.statement: The sundel bolong myth also became common in Malaysia after migrants from the archipelago brought it.
claims.statement_id: Mitos sundel bolong juga umum di Malaysia setelah dibawa imigran dari Nusantara.
claims.quote: Mitos hantu sundel bolong juga telah menjadi mitos yang umum di Malaysia setelah dibawa oleh imigran-imigran dari nusantara.

claims.statement: In archipelago lore, the sundel bolong is the restless spirit of a woman who died after being raped and then gave birth in the grave.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Nusantara, sundel bolong adalah arwah penasaran perempuan yang mati karena diperkosa lalu melahirkan anaknya di dalam kubur.
claims.quote: Dalam mitos nusantara, hantu sundel bolong adalah arwah penasaran dari wanita yang mati karena diperkosa dan kemudian melahirkan anaknya di dalam kubur.

claims.statement: It is suggested the myth was created to protect women walking alone at night in the countryside from ill-intentioned men.
claims.statement_id: Ada dugaan mitos ini diciptakan untuk melindungi perempuan yang berjalan sendirian di malam hari di pedesaan dari laki-laki berniat jahat.
claims.quote: Ada dugaan bahwa mitos ini dahulu diciptakan dan disebarkan di nusantara untuk menghindarkan wanita yang berjalan sendirian saat malam hari di pedesaan dari gangguan laki-laki yang berniat jahat

claims.statement: The film Sundelbolong (1981) by Rapi Films, directed by Sisworo Gautama Putra and starring Suzanna, is credited with popularizing the sundel bolong.
claims.statement_id: Film Sundelbolong (1981) dari Rapi Films, disutradarai Sisworo Gautama Putra dan dibintangi Suzanna, dianggap memopulerkan sundel bolong.
claims.quote: yang dianggap telah memopulerkan sundel bolong adalah film Sundelbolong (1981) dari Rapi Films yang disutradarai maestro film Sisworo Gautama Putra dan dibintangi Suzanna

claims.statement: Sundelbolong was released in 1981, and Legenda Sundel Bolong in 2007.
claims.statement_id: Film Sundelbolong dirilis pada 1981, dan Legenda Sundel Bolong pada 2007.
claims.quote: In 1981, an adult horror film, Sundelbolong was released, directed by Sisworo Gautama Putra and in 2007, Legenda Sundel Bolong was released

claims.statement: The study finds that the sundel bolong animation examined tends to normalize gender-based violence and stigmatize women's bodies.
claims.statement_id: Penelitian ini menemukan bahwa animasi sundel bolong yang dikaji cenderung menormalisasi kekerasan berbasis gender dan menstigma tubuh perempuan.
claims.quote: Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa animasi ini cenderung menormalisasi kekerasan berbasis gender, memberikan stigma negatif pada tubuh perempuan, dan mengubah pengalaman trauma menjadi sekadar tontonan hiburan.

claims.statement: Agustiningsih and Rostiyati (2019) concluded that sundel bolong films seem to justify sexual violence against women.
claims.statement_id: Agustiningsih dan Rostiyati (2019) menyimpulkan bahwa film-film sundel bolong seolah membenarkan kekerasan seksual terhadap perempuan.
claims.quote: Agustiningsih dan Rostiyati (2019) misalnya, mengkaji filmfilm Sundel Bolong dan menyimpulkan bahwa film-film tersebut seolah membenarkan kekerasan seksual yang dialami perempuan

claims.statement: Sundal generally means harlot or prostitute, and bolong in Javanese means pierced through.
claims.statement_id: Sundal umumnya berarti wanita jalang atau pelacur, dan bolong dalam bahasa Jawa berarti berlubang tembus.
claims.quote: "Sundal" umumnya merujuk pada "wanita jalang" atau "pelacur", dan "bolong" adalah bahasa Jawa yang berarti "berlubang tembus"

claims.statement: The toyol or tuyul is an undead infant of Indonesian and Malay folklore, also in other Southeast Asian mythologies, typically summoned by shamans (dukun, pawang, bomoh) through black magic, mainly to rob people, similar to the babi ngepet; it brings luck to its host and misfortune to those it meets.
claims.statement_id: Toyol atau tuyul adalah bayi mayat hidup dalam cerita rakyat Indonesia dan Melayu, juga dalam mitologi Asia Tenggara lain, yang biasa dipanggil dukun, pawang, atau bomoh dengan ilmu hitam, terutama untuk mencuri harta orang, mirip babi ngepet; ia membawa untung bagi pemiliknya dan celaka bagi yang ditemuinya.
claims.quote: A toyol or tuyul is an undead infant in Indonesian and Malay folklore. It also appears in the various other mythologies of Southeast Asia and is typically invoked as a helper by shamans (dukun, pawang, or bomoh) by means of black magic. A common use for the toyol includes using it for financial gain, where the creature robs people of their riches, making it similar to the Babi ngepet

claims.statement: Toyol (Malay) is tuyul in Indonesian, thuyul in Javanese, kecit in Sundanese; in Thai the male is kuman-thong and the female kuman-lay; a similar Philippine creature is the tiyanak.
claims.statement_id: Toyol (Melayu) disebut tuyul dalam bahasa Indonesia, thuyul dalam bahasa Jawa, kecit dalam bahasa Sunda; di Thailand yang laki-laki kuman-thong dan yang perempuan kuman-lay; makhluk serupa di Filipina disebut tiyanak.
claims.quote: The Malay word toyol is tuyul in Indonesian, thuyul in Javanese, and kecit in Sundanese. It is also known as cohen kroh in Khmer, and kwee kia in Hokkien. In Thai, the male is called kuman-thong while the female is named kuman-lay. A similar creature exists in Philippine mythology which is known as tiyanak.

claims.statement: The toyol is traditionally a near-naked toddler with sharp teeth and red eyes; the Indonesian tuyul adds green skin and pointed ears and can scale walls and roofs.
claims.statement_id: Toyol secara tradisional digambarkan seperti balita hampir telanjang, dengan gigi tajam dan mata merah; tuyul Indonesia ditambah kulit hijau dan telinga runcing, dan dapat memanjat dinding serta atap.
claims.quote: The toyol is traditionally and commonly described as looking no different from a near-naked toddler. ... the toyol is claimed to look like a normal child with the exception of sharp teeth and red eyes, but the Indonesian tuyul has the addition of green skin and pointed ears. The tuyul has the ability to scale walls and climb roofs.

claims.statement: The toyol behaves like a playful child fond of sweets, toys and clothes; it is said to steal only half of a person's valuables.
claims.statement_id: Sifat toyol dikatakan seperti anak kecil yang suka bermain dan menyukai permen, mainan, dan pakaian; konon ia hanya mencuri separuh barang berharga seseorang.
claims.quote: The toyol's behaviour and personality is typically said to be similar to that of a playful child, where it enjoys sweets, toys, and clothes.

claims.statement: Belief in the toyol serves social functions, including discipline, maintaining hierarchy and warding off outsiders.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada toyol punya fungsi sosial, antara lain sebagai alat pendisiplinan, penjaga hierarki sosial, dan pengusir orang luar.
claims.quote: Aside from the belief in the supernatural, the toyol serves a range of social functions, including acting as a disciplinary tool, to assist in maintaining social hierarchy, and to ward off perceived outsiders away from the community.

claims.statement: The wealthy and successful, even government officials, are often associated with using a toyol.
claims.statement_id: Orang kaya dan sukses, bahkan pejabat pemerintah, tidak jarang dituduh memakai toyol.
claims.quote: It is not an uncommon occurrence for people to associate those with wealth and success to having used a toyol, and this negative association is extended to even government officials.

claims.statement: Such stories are theorized as a way to reduce dissonance, letting people accept status as beyond their control; or simply a way to voice resentment.
claims.statement_id: Cerita semacam ini diteorikan sebagai cara meredam disonansi, sehingga orang dapat menerima bahwa status sosial di luar kendali mereka; atau sekadar ungkapan rasa iri.
claims.quote: These stories of corruption and amorality have been theorised to be a method of negating dissonance, where through associating social status with the supernatural, it allows for the people to believe and accept that the matter is beyond their control. On the other hand, such accusations can simply be a way of expressing one's resentment.

claims.statement: In 2006 a Kuala Pahang, Malaysia fisherman reported finding a bottled toyol on the shore, handed to the state museum.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2006 seorang nelayan dari Kuala Pahang, Malaysia, melaporkan menemukan toyol dalam botol di pantai, yang lalu diserahkan ke museum negeri.
claims.quote: In 2006, a fisherman from Kuala Pahang, Malaysia reported finding a toyol that had been enclosed in a bottle on coastal shores. The toyol was handed over to the local state museum

claims.statement: In 2019 residents of Mengwi, Badung, Bali believed a tuyul caused a resident's loss of IDR 1.4 million.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2019 warga Mengwi, Badung, Bali, percaya tuyul menjadi penyebab hilangnya uang Rp1,4 juta milik seorang warga.
claims.quote: As recently as 2019, it was reported that residents living in the Mengwi subdistrict of Badung Regency in Bali, Indonesia believed that a tuyul was the reason for why one resident had mysteriously lost IDR1.4 million.

claims.statement: Kuman-thong and kuman-lay are said to be more benevolent and, unlike the toyol, need neither sacrifices nor rituals.
claims.statement_id: Kuman-thong dan kuman-lay disebut lebih baik hati dan, berbeda dari toyol, tidak memerlukan korban atau ritual.
claims.quote: For instance, the kuman-thong and kuman-lay are said to be more benevolent, and unlike the toyol whose owner has to tame, these Thai spirits do not need neither sacrifices nor rituals in order to invoke their services.

claims.statement: In Japanese folklore, the zashiki-warashi resembles the toyol in bringing good fortune to its owners.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, zashiki-warashi mirip toyol karena dipercaya membawa keberuntungan bagi pemiliknya.
claims.quote: In Japanese folklore, the zashiki-warashi shares some similarity to the toyol where they are believed to bring good fortune to their owners.

claims.statement: Malik Selamat directed the 1980 Malay horror film Toyol; the 2011 Malaysian comedy Alamak... Toyol! also features a toyol.
claims.statement_id: Malik Selamat menyutradarai film horor Melayu Toyol (1980); film komedi Malaysia Alamak... Toyol! (2011) juga menampilkan toyol.
claims.quote: Malik Selamat directed a 1980 Malay horror film Toyol

claims.statement: The 2011 Malaysian comedy Alamak... Toyol! uses a toyol as its plot device.
claims.statement_id: Film komedi Malaysia Alamak... Toyol! (2011) menampilkan toyol sebagai penggerak cerita.
claims.quote: The 2011 Malaysian comedy film Alamak... Toyol! features a toyol as its plot device.

claims.statement: The toyol is said to steal only half of a person's valuables.
claims.statement_id: Toyol konon hanya mencuri separuh barang berharga seseorang.
claims.quote: The toyol is also said to only steal half of a person's valuable belongings.

claims.statement: Modern depictions often give the toyol a goblin-like look with green or grey skin, pointed ears and clouded eyes.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran modern sering memberi toyol rupa mirip goblin dengan kulit hijau atau abu-abu, telinga runcing, dan mata keruh.
claims.quote: Modern depictions often give the toyol a goblin-like appearance with green or grey skin, pointed ears, and clouded eyes.

claims.statement: In Malay ghost belief, the Orang Minyak ('oily man') is a supernatural being coated in shiny black grease who abducts young women at night; the legend is first mentioned in a Berita Harian (Singapore) report of 12 October 1957.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan hantu Melayu, Orang Minyak ('orang berminyak') adalah makhluk gaib berlumur minyak hitam mengilap yang menculik perempuan muda pada malam hari; legendanya pertama disebut dalam laporan surat kabar Singapura Berita Harian, 12 Oktober 1957.
claims.quote: In Malay ghost beliefs, the Orang Minyak ("oily man" in Malay) is a supernatural creature coated with shiny black grease who abducts young women by night. The legend of the figure is first mentioned in a report from the Singaporean newspaper Berita Harian dated 12 October 1957.

claims.statement: It supposedly climbs walls and grabs victims while escaping thanks to its slippery coating, first described as hair oil, later coconut oil and soot; films show it in crude oil.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon dapat memanjat dinding dan menangkap korban sambil lolos berkat lapisan licinnya, yang mula-mula disebut minyak rambut, lalu minyak kelapa dan jelaga; film menggambarkannya berlumur minyak mentah.
claims.quote: Supposedly, the creature is able to climb walls and grab victims while evading capture due to its slippery coating. The coating was first described as consisting of hair oil, before later stories evolved into it being covered in coconut oil and soot; the genre movies have it covered in crude oil

claims.statement: Many stories call it a rapist targeting only virgins; from the 1950s it was blamed for rapes, and superstitious Malay female students wore sweaty clothing to ward it off.
claims.statement_id: Banyak cerita menyebut Orang Minyak pemerkosa yang hanya menyasar perawan; sejak 1950-an ia disalahkan atas perkosaan, dan mahasiswi Melayu yang percaya takhayul memakai pakaian berkeringat untuk menangkalnya.
claims.quote: A number of stories describe the Orang Minyak as a rapist that only targets virgins. The Orang Minyak has been traditionally blamed for rapes, beginning in the 1950s, and superstitious Malay female students would attempt to ward off the creature by donning sweaty clothing

claims.statement: Some versions hold the Orang Minyak is an evil human warlock, not a supernatural being.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian versi menyebut Orang Minyak manusia penyihir jahat, bukan makhluk gaib.
claims.quote: Some versions of the legend hold that the Orang Minyak is an evil human warlock rather than a supernatural creature.

claims.statement: In the version popularized by P. Ramlee's 1958 film Sumpah Orang Minyak, he was a man cursed while trying to win back his love with magic.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi yang dipopulerkan film Sumpah Orang Minyak (1958) karya dan dibintangi P. Ramlee, Orang Minyak adalah laki-laki yang dikutuk saat mencoba merebut kembali kekasihnya dengan sihir.
claims.quote: In one version of the legend, popularised in the 1958 film Sumpah Orang Minyak (The Curse of the Oily Man) directed by and starring P. Ramlee, the Orang Minyak was a man who was cursed in an attempt to win back his love with magic.

claims.statement: In 2012 residents of Kampung Laksamana, Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia claimed to have seen and heard it.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2012 warga Kampung Laksamana di Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia, mengaku melihat dan mendengar makhluk ini.
claims.quote: In 2012, the residents in Kampung (Village) Laksamana, in Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia, claimed to have seen and heard the creature

claims.statement: Sumpah Orang Minyak was released alongside Orang Minyak and Serangan Orang Minyak (1958); this run of films raised the legend to peak fame in 1950s–60s Malaya.
claims.statement_id: Sumpah Orang Minyak dirilis bersamaan dengan Orang Minyak dan Serangan Orang Minyak (1958); rangkaian film ini melambungkan legenda itu ke puncak ketenarannya pada 1950-an dan 1960-an di Malaya.
claims.quote: was released alongside Cathay-Keris’s own Orang Minyak (The Oily Man, 1958) and Serangan Orang Minyak (The Oily Man Strikes Again, 1958) in the same year. The spate of movies catapulted the folklore legend to the peak of its notoriety and screen fame in 1950s and 1960s of Malaya.

claims.statement: Science writer Benjamin Radford called the tales rooted in myth and folklore and the creature's abilities implausible.
claims.statement_id: Penulis sains Benjamin Radford menyebut kisah ini berakar pada mitos dan cerita rakyat, dan kemampuan makhluk itu tidak masuk akal.
claims.quote: Science writer Benjamin Radford described the tales as "rooted in myth and folklore" and characterized the creature's supposed abilities as "implausible".

claims.statement: Singaporean writer Yogesh Tulsi says the crude-oil Orang Minyak represents traditional life ruined by petro-modernity.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Singapura Yogesh Tulsi berpendapat penggambaran Orang Minyak berlumur minyak mentah melambangkan cara hidup tradisional yang dirusak modernitas perminyakan.
claims.quote: Singaporean writer Yogesh Tulsi comments that the orang minyak's depictions slathered in crude oil represents traditional ways of life ruined by a "horrific petromodernity".

claims.statement: The film Orang Minyak was digitally restored by the Asian Film Archive in 2018.
claims.statement_id: Film Orang Minyak direstorasi secara digital oleh Asian Film Archive pada 2018.
claims.quote: Orang Minyak was digitally restored by the Asian Film Archive in 2018 using a 16mm black & white composite release print from its collection.

claims.statement: Vietnamese dragons (Rồng; Sino-Vietnamese: Long; 龍) are symbolic creatures of Vietnamese folklore and mythology; an ancient origin myth says the Vietnamese descend from a dragon and an Immortal.
claims.statement_id: Naga Vietnam (Rồng; Sino-Vietnam: Long; 龍) adalah makhluk simbolis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Vietnam; menurut mitos asal-usul kuno, bangsa Vietnam keturunan naga dan makhluk abadi.
claims.quote: Vietnamese dragons (Vietnamese: Rồng; chữ Nôm: 蠬/蠪; Sino-Vietnamese: Long; chữ Hán: 龍) are symbolic creatures in Vietnamese folklore and mythology. According to an ancient origin myth, the Vietnamese people are descended from a dragon and an Immortal.

claims.statement: The dragon symbolized rain for agriculture and represents the emperor and the nation's prosperity and power; like the fierce but benevolent Chinese dragon, it is a symbol of yang: universe, life, existence and growth.
claims.statement_id: Naga melambangkan pembawa hujan yang penting bagi pertanian, mewakili kaisar serta kemakmuran dan kekuatan bangsa; seperti naga Tiongkok yang galak tetapi baik hati, naga Vietnam adalah lambang yang: alam semesta, kehidupan, keberadaan, dan pertumbuhan.
claims.quote: The dragon was symbolic of bringing rain, essential for agriculture. It represents the emperor, the prosperity and power of the nation. Similar to the Chinese dragon (which has also influenced and appeared in Japan and Korea as fierce but benevolent serpentine dragons alike), the Vietnamese dragon is the symbol of yang, representing the universe, life, existence, and growth.

claims.statement: Lạc Long Quân, king of the dragonkind, married the fairy goddess Âu Cơ, who bore 100 eggs hatching into 100 sons; the eldest became king of Lạc Việt as Hùng Vương; hence the saying Con Rồng, cháu Tiên (descendants of Dragon and Immortal).
claims.statement_id: Lạc Long Quân, raja bangsa naga, menikah dengan dewi peri Âu Cơ yang melahirkan 100 telur yang menetas menjadi 100 putra; putra sulung menjadi raja Lạc Việt dan bergelar Hùng Vương; dari sinilah ungkapan Con Rồng, cháu Tiên (keturunan Naga dan Makhluk Abadi).
claims.quote: Lạc Long Quân, king of the dragonkind living near the Đông sea, married a fairy goddess, Âu Cơ who was the daughter of the birdkind emperor Đế Lai, descendant of Thần Nông. Âu Cơ bore 100 eggs, which hatched into 100 sons. The first-born son became the king of Lạc Việt, the first dynasty of Vietnam, and proclaimed himself Emperor Hùng Vương.

claims.statement: The Vietnamese dragon combines crocodile, snake, cat, rat and bird; living near rivers, the Vietnamese venerated crocodiles as thuồng luồng or Giao Long, the first Vietnamese dragon.
claims.statement_id: Citra naga Vietnam memadukan buaya, ular, kucing, tikus, dan burung; karena tinggal dekat sungai, orang Vietnam memuja buaya sebagai thuồng luồng atau Giao Long, jenis naga Vietnam pertama.
claims.quote: The Vietnamese dragon is the combined image of crocodile, snake, cat, rat and bird. Historically, the Vietnamese people lived near rivers, so they venerated crocodiles as "thuồng luồng" or "Giao Long", the first kind of Vietnamese dragon.

claims.statement: Lý-era dragons (1010–1225) have 12 body sections for the 12 months, small regular back fins and an upright head with long mane and beard but no horns; they can change the weather, are responsible for crops, and always hold a jewel.
claims.statement_id: Naga masa Lý (1010–1225) bertubuh 12 ruas yang melambangkan 12 bulan, bersirip punggung kecil teratur, berkepala tegak dengan surai panjang dan janggut, tanpa tanduk; naga ini dapat mengubah cuaca, bertanggung jawab atas panen, dan selalu menggigit permata.
claims.quote: The body has 12 sections, symbolizing 12 months in the year. On the dragon's back are small, uninterrupted, regular fins. The head, held high, is in proportion with the body, and has a long mane, beard, prominent eyes, crest on nose (pointing forwards), but no horns.

claims.statement: The Trần dragon (1225–1400) resembled the Lý dragon but was more rugged, with new arms and horns.
claims.statement_id: Naga masa Trần (1225–1400) mirip naga Lý tetapi lebih kekar, dengan tambahan lengan dan tanduk.
claims.quote: The Trần dynasty dragon was similar to that of the Lý dynasty but looked more rugged. The Trần dragon had new details: arms and horns.

claims.statement: On a Ngô-dynasty (938–965) brick from Cổ Loa, the dragon is short with a cat-like body and a fish's back fin.
claims.statement_id: Pada bata masa dinasti Ngô (938–965) dari Cổ Loa, naga bertubuh pendek seperti kucing dengan sirip punggung ikan.
claims.quote: On the brick from this period found in Cổ Loa, the dragon is short, with a cat-like body and a fish's backfin.

claims.statement: These dragons can change the weather and are responsible for crops.
claims.statement_id: Naga-naga ini dapat mengubah cuaca dan bertanggung jawab atas panen.
claims.quote: These dragons are able to change the weather, and are responsible for crops.
